recommendations: Do not treat a completed search as a completed technical record: track identity, field-level evidence, offers and visual reference separately.
Persist manufacturer MPN/GTIN with aliases; only share fields between exact same-MPN IDs after conflicting capacity, kit, finish and revision checks. Do not merge by family name.

Cross-store discovery should start with manufacturer MPN, then exact product page. Mixed colours such as white/grey describe a single physical design, not necessarily multiple variants; manufacturer imagery can resolve these current automatic false negatives.

Continue each pending SKU with manufacturer page/manual and then seller offers until either documented or a specific missing discriminator is recorded; two loosely-ranked search candidates are not an exhaustive review.
Fill compatibility fields from explicit category-specific labels and units. Text-only technical groups do not feed the compatibility engine.
Replace the opaque detailLevel flag with the list of missing fields relevant to the selected build; complete dimensions do not validate price, BIOS, QVL or a precise radiator assembly.
Keep GPU TBP separate from recommended system PSU and CPU TDP separate from electrical budget. Keep SPD/VPP distinct from tested RAM voltage and on-die ECC distinct from host ECC.

Build shared visual geometry for manufacturer chassis/family, then use per-SKU dimensions, fan count, finish and photographic landmarks. Reuse shapes only when visual evidence confirms shared hardware.
